sections.h2: What are the basic tenant rights in Maine when a landlord wants to sell?
sections.html:
A sale does not cancel a tenant's rights in Maine. The tenant keeps the protections that come with the tenancy, and the landlord still has to follow the same notice, deposit and court rules. The Maine Attorney General's tenant rights page covers the main ones: a safe and habitable home, written notice of rent increases, reasonable notice before entry, a deposit returned on time, and no eviction without a court order.

Two kinds of rental matter most. A tenant with a written lease holds a fixed term and the lease controls the notice rules. A tenant without a lease, or with a lease that says nothing about notice, is a tenant at will and can be asked to leave on written notice under 14 M.R.S. §6002. Knowing which kind of tenancy you have is the first step before you list a rental or accept an offer.

sections.h2: Can a landlord evict a tenant just because the house is being sold?
sections.html:
Not on the landlord's say-so. A landlord must go to court to remove a tenant, and self-help such as changing locks, blocking entry or shutting off utilities is illegal. The Attorney General's page says the first step is a notice to quit, which is not a court order and does not by itself require the tenant to leave.

For a tenant at will, either side can end the tenancy with at least 30 days' written notice, and if rent has been paid through a date later than the end of the 30 days, the notice must expire on or after that date. The notice has to advise the tenant of the right to contest the termination in court. Starting January 1, 2024, a landlord must attach the Judicial Branch's form notice to any notice terminating a tenancy (14 M.R.S. §6001, subsection 7).

If the tenant has an unexpired lease, the lease term governs, and if a lease expired less than 7 days ago, no notice is required. A buyer who wants the house vacant should price that wait into the deal.

sections.h2: What does a buyer take when a rental is sold?
sections.html:
A third-party buyer cannot start an eviction case against a tenant at will unless the tenant received proper §6002 notice from the grantor or the grantee. That limit is in §6001, subsection 2, and it is the rule most relevant to a sale.

In plain terms, the buyer cannot skip the notice step just because ownership changed. Either the seller serves a proper notice before closing, or the buyer serves one after. If a foreclosure is pending or a judgment has been entered, a bona fide tenancy may end only under the federal Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act of 2009 (§6001, subsection 1-A).

  • Sellers who want a vacant house should serve notice early and keep proof of service.
  • Buyers who will keep the tenant should ask for the lease, the rent history and the deposit amount.
  • A cash buyer who accepts the tenant as is can close without waiting for the unit to empty.

The sources we reviewed do not say how a security deposit is handed over at closing, so settle that in writing in the purchase agreement and have an attorney review it.

sections.h2: How do security deposits work in Maine?
sections.html:
A deposit cannot exceed two months' rent. Section 6032 sets the cap, and the Attorney General adds that the landlord must hold the deposit in a separate account during the tenancy.

After the tenancy ends, §6033 requires the landlord to return the full deposit, or return the balance with an itemized written statement, within the period in a written agreement (not more than 30 days) or within 21 days for a tenancy at will. Deductions can cover unpaid rent, damage and storage or disposal of left-behind property, but not normal wear and tear.

RuleMaine standardSource
Deposit capTwo months' rent14 M.R.S. §6032
Return deadline, written agreementAs stated, up to 30 days§6033
Return deadline, tenancy at will21 days§6033
Missed deadlineLandlord loses the right to withhold any part§6033
Wrongful retentionTwice the amount, plus fees, after 7 days' notice§6034

In a lawsuit under §6034 the landlord must prove that withholding was not wrongful. That makes clean records matter when a rental changes hands.

sections.h2: What notice must a landlord give for rent increases?
sections.html:
Tenants at will must receive 75 days' written notice for increases over 10% and 45 days' notice for smaller increases. The Attorney General's advisory says the notice rule covers all rental housing, including rented mobile homes, tenants cannot waive it, and cumulative increases within 12 months count toward the 10% line.

A tenant with an unexpired lease cannot have rent raised above the lease amount. Mobile home parks have their own law that requires 90 days' notice for all rent and fee increases. A tenant who is charged without proper notice may recover rent, interest and reasonable attorney's fees, and can file a complaint with the Attorney General's office.

This affects sellers because a new owner who wants to raise rent must follow the same notice clock. A buyer underwriting a rental should assume the first increase will take at least 45 days to take effect.

sections.h2: Can a landlord enter to show the house to a buyer?
sections.html:
Yes, with reasonable notice. The Attorney General says 24 hours' notice is presumed reasonable, entry must happen at reasonable times, and a tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry for showings to prospective buyers, lenders, tenants or contractors.

  • Give written notice for each showing, and keep a copy.
  • Group showings on fewer days to avoid a harassment complaint.
  • Emergencies are the exception to the notice rule.

Retaliation is the risk. Under §6001 there is a rebuttable presumption of retaliation when the tenant engaged in protected activity, such as a habitability complaint, within 6 months before the landlord's action, and no writ of possession may issue unless that presumption is rebutted.

sections.h2: What repairs and conditions must a Maine landlord handle before selling?
sections.html:
All rented housing must be fit for human habitation, and an unrepaired problem can follow the property into a sale dispute. A tenant can sue for repairs only after showing that the condition endangers health or safety, the tenant did not cause it, written notice was given, the tenant was current on rent, and the landlord failed to fix it in a reasonable time.

Repair and deduct is available when the repair costs less than $500 or half the monthly rent, whichever is greater. The tenant gives written notice, and if the landlord does not act within 14 days (or promptly in an emergency) the tenant may arrange the repair and deduct the reasonable cost. If the landlord supplies heat, the system must maintain 68 degrees Fahrenheit when it is 20 degrees below zero outside. Bedbug reports require an inspection within 5 days and a pest control contact within 10 days.

Under §6002, subsection 3, a tenant sued for nonpayment can raise an unrepaired habitability violation the landlord knew about, and a court that finds the unit unfit can reduce the rent owed to fair rental value.

sections.h2: How does a Maine eviction case run if a tenant will not leave?
sections.html:
A landlord files a Forcible Entry and Detainer action after the notice to quit expires. The Maine Judicial Branch guide for nonpayment cases lays out the steps, and §6004 requires a plain-language form notice to be attached to the summons and complaint for residential tenants.

StepWhat happens
Notice to quit7 days for nonpayment when rent is 7 or more days late, or 30 days for a no-cause tenancy at will
Court formsComplaint, summons and information sheet; $100 filing fee, $5 per summons
ServiceBy the sheriff, at least 14 days before the hearing
HearingMediation is available at the court on the hearing day
Writ of possessionCan issue 7 days after judgment; tenant has 48 hours after service

A nonpayment tenant who pays all rent due plus fees before the writ issues keeps the tenancy. Back rent is a separate case, often in Small Claims Court. For a seller, the notice, service and writ periods alone add up to several weeks, so a buyer who needs the house empty should expect to wait.

sections.h2: Which sellers of Maine rentals should look at a cash sale?
sections.html: Owners with a tenant who will not leave, a lease that runs past the planned closing, or a deposit dispute may find that a traditional sale is hard to time around occupancy and condition. Cash Home Buyers buys Maine houses as-is, and you can ask us about a house with a tenant in it. We do not quote a price until we have seen the property and the lease. Our Maine property tax guide and probate guide cover the other issues that often come with a rental sale.

faqs.q: How much notice does a Maine landlord need to give to end a tenancy at will?
faqs.a: At least 30 days' written notice under 14 M.R.S. §6002, or 7 days for stated causes such as rent 7 or more days late. The notice must say the tenant may contest it in court.

faqs.q: Does a lease end when the landlord sells the property?
faqs.a: The sources we reviewed do not say that a sale ends a lease. A third-party buyer cannot evict a tenant at will unless the tenant received proper §6002 notice from the seller or the buyer.

faqs.q: How much can a landlord charge for a security deposit in Maine?
faqs.a: No more than two months' rent. The landlord must return it or send an itemized statement within 30 days under a written agreement, or within 21 days for a tenancy at will.

faqs.q: How much notice is required for a rent increase?
faqs.a: 75 days' written notice for increases over 10% and 45 days for smaller increases for tenants at will. Mobile home parks require 90 days.

faqs.q: Can a landlord shut off utilities or change the locks?
faqs.a: No. Landlords must go to court to remove a tenant, and self-help evictions are illegal in Maine.

faqs.q: Can a tenant refuse to let a buyer see the home?
faqs.a: A tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry for showings to prospective buyers, and 24 hours' notice is presumed reasonable.

faqs.q: How long does a Maine eviction take after the notice to quit?
faqs.a: The hearing must be at least 14 days after service, and a writ of possession can issue 7 days after judgment, after which the tenant has 48 hours to leave.
